arxiv-1901-11293.title: Exact nonequilibrium quantum observable statistics: A large-deviation approach
arxiv-1901-11293.creator: Stefano Gherardini
arxiv-1901-11293.description: Abstract The exact statistics of an arbitrary quantum observable is analytically obtained. Due to the probabilistic nature of a sequence of intermediate measurements and stochastic fluctuations induced by the interaction with the environment, the measurement outcomes at the end of the system’s evolution are random variables.

arxiv-2105-06843.title: H 2 formation on interstellar grains and the fate of reaction energy Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2105-06843.creator: Stefano Pantaleone, Joan Enrique-Romero, Cecilia Ceccarelli, Stefano Ferrero, Nadia Balucani, Albert Rimola, Piero Ugliengo
arxiv-2105-06843.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Stefano Pantaleone, Joan Enrique-Romero, Cecilia Ceccarelli, Stefano Ferrero, Nadia Balucani, Albert Rimola, Piero Ugliengo. Molecular hydrogen is the most abundant molecular species in the Universe. While no doubts exist that it is mainly formed on the interstellar dust grain surfaces, many details of this process remain poorly known.

arxiv-2106-09386.title: Two-fluid single-column modelling of Rayleigh-Bénard convection as a step towards multi-fluid modelling of atmospheric convection
arxiv-2106-09386.creator: Daniel Shipley, Hilary Weller, Peter Clark, William McIntyre
arxiv-2106-09386.description: Abstract Multi-fluid models have recently been proposed as an approach to improving the representation of convection in weather and climate models. This is an attractive framework as it is fundamentally dynamical, removing some of the assumptions of mass-flux convection schemes which are invalid at current model resolutions.

arxiv-2306-01454.title: NuSTAR investigation of X-ray variability and hard X-ray spectral properties in IGR J16320-4751 and IGR J16479-4514 2022 NuSTAR investigation of X-ray variability and hard X-ray spectral properties in IGR J16320-4751 and IGR J16479-4514 – References
arxiv-2306-01454.creator: Varun, Gayathri, Raman
arxiv-2306-01454.description: Abstract We present the results obtained from a comprehensive timing and spectral study of two high mass X-ray binary sources using NuSTAR observations. arxiv-2311-05528.title: The impact of decreasing horizontal grid spacing on the simulation of the mountain boundary layer in the hectometric range
arxiv-2311-05528.creator: Brigitta Goger, Anurag Dipankar
arxiv-2311-05528.description: Abstract The horizontal grid spacing of numerical weather prediction models keeps decreasing towards the hectometric range. We perform limited-area simulations with the ICON model across horizontal grid spacings (1 km, 500 m, 250 m, 125 m) in the Inn Valley, Austria, and evaluate the model with observations from the CROSSINN measurement campaign.

arxiv-2506-03847.creator: Hugo Alcaraz-Herrera, Michail-Antisthenis Tsompanas, Andrew Adamatzky, Igor Balaz
arxiv-2506-03847.description: Abstract Soft robots have proven to outperform traditional robots in applications related to propagation in geometrically constrained environments. Designing these robots and their controllers is an intricate task, since their building materials exhibit non-linear properties. Human designs may be biased; hence, alternative designing processes should be considered.

pmc-11635121.title: Direct Initiation of Levodopa–Carbidopa Intestinal Gel Infusion After a Positive Levodopa Challenge Test in Advanced Parkinson's Disease
pmc-11635121.creator: Vili Viljaharju, Tuomas Mertsalmi, K Amande M Pauls, Maija Koivu, Johanna Eerola‐Rautio, Marianne Udd, Eero Pekkonen
pmc-11635121.description: IntroductionLevodopa–carbidopa intestinal gel (LCIG) is an established treatment option in advanced Parkinson's disease (PD). LCIG treatment is usually initiated with a nasojejunal tube (NJT) test phase before percutaneous endoscopic transgastric jejunostomy (PEG‐J) tube installation. However, some centers have used direct initiation with PEG‐J. Data comparing these approaches are scarce.

pmc-12668201.title: Leveraging productivity indicators for anomaly detection in swine breeding herds with unsupervised learning
pmc-12668201.creator: Mafalda Pedro Mil-Homens, Chong Wang, Giovani Trevisan, Fernanda Dórea, Daniel C. L. Linhares, Derald Holtkamp, Gustavo S. Silva
pmc-12668201.description: IntroductionIn swine disease surveillance, obtaining labeled data for supervised learning models can be challenging because many farms lack standardized diagnostic routines and consistent health monitoring systems. Unsupervised learning is particularly suitable in such scenarios because it does not require labeled data, allowing for detecting anomalies without predefined labels.

pmc-13005980.title: The Diagnostic and Prognostic Value of Procalcitonin and High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein in Early-Stage Burn Sepsis: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13005980.creator: Guo-Xun Yang, Zhong-Fei Cui, Shan-Shan Zhao, Zhi-Qiang Wu, Cai Zhu, Ting Que, Shu-Qian Dou, Xin Wang, Xiao-Ling Wang, Qing-Jiang Chen, Xiao-Bo Liu, Wenjun Liu

pmc-13334776.title: Surface-modified FeCo nanoparticles: magnetic dilution and structure–magnetism relationships
pmc-13334776.creator: Bui The Huy, Jong Won Chung, The-Long Phan, Tran Thi Ngoc Nha, Le Thi Tuyet Ngan, Pham Thanh Phong
pmc-13334776.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). FeCo nanoparticles with controlled composition and tailored surface chemistry were synthesized via an ultrasound-assisted co-precipitation method and subsequently functionalized with zirconium oxide (ZrO2), polyethylene glycol, and chitosan using precipitation, adsorption, and surface coupling strategies, respectively. Structural and morphological analyses by X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy confirm the formation of crystalline body-centered cubic (bcc) FeCo nanoparticles with preserved core structure after surface modification, while energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy verifies the successful incorporation of constituent elements without detectable impurity phases.

pmc-13365280.title: Therapeutic potential of Leonotis leonurus and Mentha longifolia in depression: insights from network pharmacology and molecular dynamics stimulation-based study
pmc-13365280.creator: Caroline Mooki, Oladunni M. Ayodele, Saheed Sabiu, Adeyemi O. Aremu, Makhotso Lekhooa
pmc-13365280.description: Medicinal plants offer promising multi-target therapeutic agents due to their diverse bioactive compounds. This study explored LC–MS profiling, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation to investigate the potential antidepressant-related mechanisms of Leonotis leonurus and Mentha longifolia. A total of 20 and 15 compounds were identified in L. leonurus and M. longifolia, respectively.

pmc-13477170.title: Beyond Single Biomarkers: A Multidimensional Risk Score for Improved Post-Transplant Prognosis Prediction in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
pmc-13477170.creator: Xiao-yong Ye, Simeng Lei, Guang Jia, Qiang He, Zhili Ji, Jun Ma
pmc-13477170.description: IntroductionInflammation- and nutrition-related biomarkers are associated with prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but most studies have focused on single markers. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a multidimensional inflammatory-nutritional risk score (RS) for predicting post-transplant outcomes in HCC patients.
